tasks.title: shared enforcement plumbing (Principal, PermissionChecker protocol, requires_permission decorator)
implementation_steps: Create the src/backend/shared/ package (additive; __init__.py exporting Principal, PermissionChecker, requires_permission).
Create src/backend/shared/principal.py defining the Principal model: Principal(user_id: UUID | None = None, session_token: str | None = None); Principal() is the system principal.
Define the structural PermissionChecker protocol: require_permission(user_id, permission, session_token=None) -> None and has_permission(user_id, permission, session_token=None) -> bool.

Implement the requires_permission decorator: it wraps an enforced service method, extracts the trailing principal parameter, and (when a PermissionChecker is injected into the owning service) calls checker.require_permission(principal.user_id, permission_key, session_token=principal.session_token) at entry; a denial raises and propagates. When no checker is injected (standalone mode), the method runs open.
The decorator must NOT import backend.permissions: it calls the injected checker and lets the denial propagate (no circular import between backend.shared and backend.permissions).
design_constraints: ADR-070: the shared enforcement plumbing lives in src/backend/shared/ (generic authorization plumbing, no feature-specific business logic; avoids the usermanagement <-> permissions circular import).
ADR-071: the decorator requires the permission at entry; the principal is the trailing parameter with a default (the system principal).
The decorator does not import backend.permissions (it calls the injected checker and lets it propagate).
completion_gates: Acceptance test for AC-032 (principal defaults and fields) passes.
Unit test for the requires_permission decorator (deny propagates, allow proceeds, standalone open) passes.
No circular import between backend.shared and backend.permissions.

tasks.title: usermanagement multi-role amendment (User.roles list, RoleStore, set_roles/add_role/remove_role, last-admin guard, member->user rename, data migration)
implementation_steps: Change User.role: str -> User.roles: list[str] (non-empty) in the model, repository, and events.
Change UserCreate.role -> UserCreate.roles (non-empty list) and UserRead.role -> UserRead.roles.
Add the structural RoleStore protocol + StaticRoleStore(("admin", "user")) default; validate role existence against the RoleStore on create/assignment (unknown role -> InvalidRoleError).
Add UserManager methods set_roles / add_role / remove_role; preserve set_role as set_roles([role]) (replace semantics).

Extend the last-admin guard to every assignment path (set_role, set_roles, remove_role, delete_user, deactivate_user); an "active admin" is an active user whose roles include admin; add_role cannot remove admin and is never rejected by the guard.
Change event fields: UserRoleChanged.old_roles / new_roles (lists); UserCreated.roles (list).
Rename the role value member -> user.
Add the alembic data migration: rewrite role values (member -> user) and convert the single role column to a role list (idempotent; no data loss).
Update all consumers and tests within the change (the breaking change is fixed in-scope).
design_constraints: ADR-072: the user-management amendment is breaking and fixed in scope (User.role -> User.roles list; RoleStore; set_roles/add_role/remove_role; set_role preserved as set_roles([role]); last-admin guard on every path; member -> user rename; alembic data migration).
The last-admin guard is preserved on every role-assignment path (no bypass).
The data migration must be idempotent and must not lose data.
completion_gates: Acceptance tests for AC-033, AC-034, AC-035, AC-036, AC-037 pass.
Property test for INV-003 (last-admin invariant) passes.
The alembic data migration applies cleanly to a fresh and an existing database.

tasks.title: permissions foundation (models, errors, events, catalog, repository ABCs + SQLite + in-memory, feature_settings)
implementation_steps: Create the src/backend/permissions/ package (models.py, errors.py, events.py, catalog.py, repositories.py, feature_settings.py, service.py, __init__.py).
Define the SQLModel models: Role (role, description, is_builtin, created_at), RolePermission (role, permission), SystemPrincipalPermission (permission).

Define the error hierarchy in errors.py rooted at AuthorizationError: PermissionDeniedError (user_id, permission, reason), RoleNotFoundError (role), RoleAlreadyExistsError (role), RoleInUseError (role), RoleProtectedError (role), UnknownPermissionError (permission). No collision with the built-in PermissionError.
Define the events: PermissionDenied (user_id, permission, reason), RoleCreated (role), RoleDeleted (role), RolePermissionsChanged (role, added, removed). Events carry non-sensitive data only.
Define the PermissionCatalog (static, closed set; the register_actions mechanism; validates action keys against ^[a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z0-9_-]+$ and feature wildcards <feature>.*).
Define the repository ABCs (RoleRepository, GrantRepository, SystemPrincipalRepository) + the SQLModel/SQLite implementations + the in-memory implementations (tests/DI).
Define feature_settings.py: register_settings(registry) registering permissions.system_principal (LIST, default = the bootstrap system set).
Export the public API in __init__.py (the NFR-003 contract).
design_constraints: ADR-069: the permissions feature is standalone (depends only on repository ABCs, UserManager, and a structural session-lookup seam; no third-party dependency).
ADR-074: the catalog is static (a closed set derived from feature declarations at startup); roles are runtime-managed.
ADR-075: the error hierarchy is rooted at AuthorizationError (no collision with the built-in PermissionError); PermissionDeniedError carries user_id/permission/reason; role errors carry role.
The catalog validates action keys and feature wildcards; duplicate keys raise ValueError.
completion_gates: Acceptance test for AC-026 (error context attributes) passes.
The public API is exported (NFR-003 contract).

tasks.title: permissions check core (has_permission/require_permission, fail-closed, admin wildcard, multi-role union, session validation, system principal, tracing, singleton)
implementation_steps: Implement PermissionService.has_permission(user_id, permission, session_token=None) -> bool and require_permission(user_id, permission, session_token=None) -> None (raises PermissionDeniedError on denial).

Implement the fail-closed check: malformed permission -> deny (malformed_permission); unknown permission (not in the catalog) -> deny (unknown_permission); unknown user -> deny (unknown_user); user lookup that raises -> deny (storage_error); inactive user -> deny (inactive_user); unknown/revoked/expired session -> deny (invalid_session); a session belonging to a different user -> deny (session_principal_mismatch).
Implement the admin implicit wildcard: a user whose roles include admin is granted every catalog permission without an explicit grant.
Implement the non-admin (user) role starting with zero permissions (permissions come only from dynamic grants).
Implement the multi-role union: the effective permission set is the union of the roles' explicit grants, including feature-wildcard matches.
Implement the live user lookup (no caching; role and activity changes take effect on the next check, no re-login).

Implement session validation via the structural SessionLookup protocol (get_by_token_hash returns a SessionRecord or None): unknown/revoked/expired -> invalid_session; a session belonging to a different user -> session_principal_mismatch; an unavailable lookup -> storage_error; an omitted token skips validation.

Implement the system principal: user_id=None is granted the configurable system permission set (stored in system_principal_permissions, live read); set_system_permissions / get_system_permissions manage it (an unknown permission -> UnknownPermissionError; a feature wildcard is allowed).
Apply @logged_class(include_args=False) tracing; log every denial at WARNING with user_id, permission, reason (never the session token).
Implement the module singleton get_permission_service() / reset_permission_service().
Publish the PermissionDenied event on every denial (the publisher is optional).
design_constraints: ADR-069: the check depends only on the repository ABCs, UserManager, and the structural session-lookup seam.
ADR-073: session validation runs through the structural SessionLookup protocol; the session token never appears in log records, events, or error messages.
ADR-075: fail-closed is a hard invariant (every undeterminable check denies); an inactive user is denied all permissions even with admin.
The check path is thread-safe (REQ-027); the session token never appears in any log record (REQ-028, NFR-002).
completion_gates: Acceptance tests for AC-002, AC-003, AC-012, AC-013, AC-017, AC-018, AC-019, AC-020, AC-021, AC-022, AC-039 pass.
Property tests for INV-001, INV-002, INV-005 pass.
Unit edge tests for EDGE-001, EDGE-002, EDGE-003, EDGE-004, EDGE-005, EDGE-006, EDGE-007, EDGE-009, EDGE-011, EDGE-020, EDGE-021, EDGE-024, EDGE-025 pass.
The check is fail-closed (INV-002).

tasks.title: permissions role CRUD + dynamic grants (create_role/delete_role + guards, grant/revoke, idempotency, role events)
implementation_steps: Implement create_role / list_roles / delete_role (backed by the roles table).

Implement the role deletion guards: built-in roles (admin, user) -> RoleProtectedError; a role assigned to any user -> RoleInUseError (the check uses the multi-role UserRead from T-002); deleting an unknown role -> RoleNotFoundError.

Implement grant_permission / revoke_permission / get_role_permissions (backed by the role_permissions table; validated against the catalog: an action key or a feature wildcard; an unknown permission -> UnknownPermissionError; an unknown role -> RoleNotFoundError).
Implement grant idempotency: granting an already-granted permission is a no-op (no duplicate row); revoking an absent grant is a no-op.
Implement the role events: RoleCreated, RoleDeleted, RolePermissionsChanged (on grant/revoke).
Make role/grant changes thread-safe (no partial state; consistent with the final state).
design_constraints: ADR-074: roles are runtime-managed; dynamic grants in the role_permissions table; grants are validated against the closed catalog and are idempotent; the admin role is an implicit wildcard; the user role starts with zero permissions; live lookups with no caching.
ADR-075: the role errors carry the role context; a role assigned to any user cannot be deleted (RoleInUseError).
The 'role assigned to any user' check uses the multi-role UserRead (T-002).
completion_gates: Acceptance tests for AC-001, AC-004, AC-005, AC-007, AC-008, AC-009, AC-010, AC-011, AC-038 pass.
Property tests for INV-004, INV-006 pass.
Unit edge tests for EDGE-008, EDGE-010, EDGE-012, EDGE-013, EDGE-014, EDGE-015, EDGE-016, EDGE-017, EDGE-018, EDGE-019 pass.
Grants are idempotent (EDGE-018, EDGE-019).

tasks.title: permissions assignment pass-throughs + settings alias sync (delegating to UserManager, SettingChanged subscription)
implementation_steps: Implement the assignment pass-throughs: assign_role / add_role / remove_role / set_roles (delegating to the corresponding UserManager method; the permission service never mutates user roles directly; an unknown role is validated against the role store before delegation -> RoleNotFoundError).
Preserve the last-admin guard on the pass-throughs (the delegation propagates LastAdminError; the user's roles are unchanged).

Implement the settings alias sync: a SettingChanged subscription updates the system-set table when permissions.system_principal is written; set_system_permissions syncs the registry key (best-effort).
Implement the no-publisher mode (all operations work normally without a publisher; no events, no errors).
Implement the in-memory repositories + the full service API working without SQLite (the singleton get_permission_service() / reset_permission_service()).
design_constraints: ADR-069: role assignment is delegated to UserManager (the permission service never mutates user roles directly).
REQ-019: the settings alias sync is best-effort (a registry write updates the table via the SettingChanged subscription; set_system_permissions syncs the key).
The pass-throughs validate against the role store before delegation (EDGE-026).
completion_gates: Acceptance tests for AC-014, AC-015, AC-016, AC-023, AC-024, AC-025, AC-028 pass.
Unit edge test for EDGE-026 (assignment unknown role) passes.
The last-admin guard is preserved on the pass-throughs (AC-015).

tasks.title: permissions persistence (alembic migration for roles/grants/system tables + seeds) + performance contract
implementation_steps: Create the alembic migration for the roles, role_permissions, and system_principal_permissions tables (SQLModel/SQLite) behind the repository ABCs.
Seed the built-in roles (admin, user, both is_builtin=True) and the bootstrap system set in the migration.
Verify the SQLite repositories work on the same file after the migration.

Implement the performance contract: a check (has_permission / require_permission) completes in < 5 ms (median) in-process, including the user/role/grant SQLite lookups and @logged tracing, measured with the synchronous console sink active.
design_constraints: ADR-069: the persistence is behind the repository ABCs (SQLModel/SQLite).
REQ-029: the performance is measured against a local SQLite database with the shared logging feature at default INFO level and the synchronous console sink active.
The migration seeds the built-in roles and the bootstrap system set (REQ-022).
completion_gates: Integration test for AC-027 (migration seeds roles and system set) passes.
Contract test for AC-040 / NFR-001 (check latency < 5 ms median) passes.

tasks.title: cross-cutting enforcement integration + composition root wiring (PermissionService as the shared PermissionChecker)
implementation_steps: Wire the composition root (src/main.py): create the PermissionService and inject it as the shared PermissionChecker into all six services at startup.
Call all six features' register_actions(catalog) at startup so the catalog contains exactly the 60 keys of the initial catalog table, grouped by the six features.

Verify the exempt login flow: login is exempt (no check on login itself); the login flow succeeds for a zero-permission user (the internal user-management/mail calls are evaluated against the bootstrap system set).

ADR-071: the exempt set is declared but not enforced.
